q: Polki or diamond jewellery: what should I wear for the wedding, reception and sangeet?
a: A simple plan works well: Polki for the wedding ceremony with a heavy bridal lehenga, diamond jewellery for the reception in a lighter outfit, and lighter Polki or diamond pieces for the sangeet and mehendi. Choose one hero necklace per function so the looks feel different. We help brides plan every function at our Parle Point showroom - WhatsApp +91 75674 00099.

q: How do I match jewellery to a heavily embroidered lehenga without overdoing it?
a: Pick one hero piece, usually the necklace, and keep the rest in proportion. Echo one stone colour from the embroidery, keep earrings lighter if the neckline is busy, and skip extra layers where the work is heaviest. Bring a photo of your lehenga to our showroom and we will try pieces against it with you.

q: What jewellery does a bride need from the wedding day to the reception?
a: Most brides plan a main necklace set with earrings, a maang tikka or matha patti, bangles or kadas, rings and a nath for the wedding, then a lighter necklace or choker with earrings for the reception and smaller sets for the sangeet and mehendi. Make a list function by function and see which pieces can be worn twice. Custom bridal pieces from our own manufacturing unit take about 3 weeks (simple designs can be faster), so plan early.

q: What jewellery suits a velvet, emerald, wine or navy lehenga for a winter wedding?
a: Rich jewel tones look best with warm gold, Polki and uncut diamonds, or emeralds and pearls that pick up the colour of the outfit. Keep one strong necklace and let the velvet stay the backdrop. You can see Polki and diamond sets against your own outfit colour at our showroom in Parle Point, Surat.

q: Which statement piece should I wear with a plain or minimal organza lehenga?
a: Choose one focal piece, such as a Polki choker, a diamond necklace or a pair of statement earrings, and keep everything else light. A minimal outfit lets a single piece stand out, so pick the one that suits your neckline. We can show you options from our collection or make one to order.

q: How do I get a layered royal bridal look with Polki, emeralds and pearls without it looking too heavy?
a: Build the look in steps: a maang tikka or matha patti, one layered necklace instead of several separate ones, and kadas that match. Space the layers so each one shows, and ask for lighter construction so the set stays comfortable through long functions. Our own manufacturing unit can adjust weight, length and clasps to suit you.

q: What jewellery should I wear with a tissue or silk saree for my wedding reception?
a: A diamond or light Polki necklace with matching earrings suits a saree well, because the drape and pallu leave the neckline open. Keep the necklace length clear of the pallu and choose earrings that frame the face. These pieces can also be worn again at family functions after the wedding.

q: What jewellery suits a floral or multicolour embroidered lehenga in blush, mint or mehendi green?
a: Soft floral colours pair well with Polki, uncut diamonds, pearls or emeralds. Pick one hero piece and keep the colours of the stones close to one shade in the embroidery so the outfit stays the focus. We can help you match pieces to your lehenga photo in the showroom.

q: What jewellery should I wear with a mirror-work or sequin lehenga for the sangeet or a night reception?
a: When the outfit already shines, choose fewer pieces with a clean shape: statement earrings or a structured diamond or Polki necklace rather than many layers. This keeps the look balanced under evening lights. Visit our Parle Point showroom to try options with your outfit photo.

q: Which maang tikka or matha patti suits my face shape and hairstyle?
a: A single drop tikka suits most faces and a centre parting; a matha patti works well with a broader forehead and a low bun; a passa on one side suits side partings and modern looks. Check the weight and the hook or clasp so it stays in place through the day. Try a few styles at our showroom to see what suits you.

q: What is the difference between CVD and HPHT lab-grown diamonds, and is the method on the report?
a: CVD and HPHT are the two main ways diamonds are grown in a laboratory: CVD builds the crystal layer by layer from a carbon gas, and HPHT recreates high pressure and temperature. Both produce real diamond. Grading reports for lab-grown diamonds state that the stone is laboratory-grown, and many also note the growth method and any post-growth treatment; read the report details, and we will go through yours with you.

q: Can I wear my diamond ring every day?
a: Yes, a well-set diamond ring can be worn daily. Take it off for the gym, heavy housework, swimming and when using chemicals or creams, and get the prongs checked once or twice a year. Bring your ring to our showroom and we will check the setting.

q: Which solitaire ring setting is best for daily wear and for long fingers or small hands?
a: For daily wear, a lower setting with sturdy prongs or a bezel catches less on clothes. Oval, pear and marquise shapes make fingers look longer, and a slimmer band suits small hands. Try several settings on your own hand at our showroom before you decide.

q: What jewellery looks best with an ivory or off-white lehenga?
a: Ivory is a clean base, so the jewellery can lead: Polki and uncut diamonds set in gold, pearls with emeralds, or a diamond choker with a long necklace. Add one colour through the stones if you want contrast. We can show you combinations from our Polki and diamond collection.

q: How do I style a necklace with a double dupatta or cape lehenga so the jewellery is still seen?
a: Choose a choker or a short necklace that sits above the drape, and keep a longer haar only if it can lie clear of the dupatta. Earrings and a maang tikka become more important because they frame the face. Our own manufacturing unit can adjust necklace lengths and clasps to suit your outfit.

q: Which jewellery goes with a sequin or crystal net lehenga without clashing?
a: Keep the jewellery soft and clean so it does not compete with the shine of the fabric: uncut or rose-cut diamonds, one hero necklace and slim earrings. Avoid many layers on a heavily embellished outfit. Try options against your outfit photo at our Parle Point showroom.

q: What jewellery should I wear with a gown or indo-western outfit for my engagement or cocktail night?
a: A diamond choker, a solitaire pendant or statement diamond earrings suit most gown necklines. Match the necklace to the neckline: chokers for strapless and off-shoulder, pendants for V-necks. Every piece we sell comes with its grading report and a BIS HUID hallmark on the gold.

q: What jewellery does a Gujarati bride wear with a panetar, gharchola or Banarasi saree?
a: A Gujarati bride often wears a rani haar or long necklace with a choker, a nath, a maang tikka or matha patti, earrings and bangles alongside her chudo. Polki and gold-set uncut diamond sets suit the red and white of the panetar and gharchola well. We make Polki and bridal sets in our own manufacturing unit in Surat - visit us at Parle Point or WhatsApp +91 75674 00099.

q: How do I choose kadas and bangles to wear with my chooda and bridal lehenga?
a: Keep the kadas in proportion to the chooda and the necklace: one or two strong kadas on each wrist balance a heavy set more easily than many thin ones. Match the metal and stones to your necklace. Each gold kada carries its own BIS HUID, which we show you against the bill.

q: Is a diamond certificate the same as a hallmark?
a: No. A diamond grading report from IGI, EGL or TGL describes the diamonds, while the BIS HUID hallmark confirms the purity of the gold. A good piece of diamond jewellery comes with both, and you can verify the HUID in the BIS Care app and the report number on the laboratory's website.

q: How do I know the stone I am buying is a diamond and not moissanite or a simulant?
a: Ask for the grading report, check that the report number laser-inscribed on the stone matches the report under a 10x loupe, and make sure the invoice names the stone. Some simple testers cannot tell moissanite from diamond, so the report and inscription are the reliable proof. We show you both in our showroom before you pay.

q: What does total carat weight mean on diamond earrings, a necklace or a bangle?
a: Total carat weight is the combined weight of all the diamonds in the piece, not the size of one stone. A pair of earrings marked 1 carat total, for example, has about half a carat in each earring. Our reports and invoices list the total weight, the number of diamonds and their quality.

q: Where is the BIS hallmark stamped on a ring, pendant, earring or bangle?
a: It is usually on the inside of a ring's band, on the back or the bail of a pendant, on the post or back of an earring, and on the inside of a bangle or kada. The mark has the BIS logo, the purity grade and a six-character HUID. We can show it to you under a loupe and match it to your bill.

q: How do I clean and store Polki and Kundan jewellery at home?
a: Wipe it gently with a soft dry cloth after wearing, keep it away from water, perfume and creams, and store each piece separately in a soft pouch or lined box. Do not soak it or rub the stones hard. Bring heavy sets to our showroom for professional cleaning.

q: Where in Surat can I see certified natural and lab-grown solitaires under a loupe before I buy?
a: At Vaishnavi Jewels, 120, Rajhans Ornate - High Street Retail Mall, Parle Point, Surat. We show you each solitaire under a loupe with its GIA or IGI report and the matching laser inscription before you pay. Visit us or WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 to book a time.

q: Which diamond shape looks biggest and suits a small hand or short fingers?
a: Elongated shapes such as oval, pear and marquise usually look larger for their carat weight and make fingers look longer. A slim band also helps on smaller hands. The grading report confirms the shape, measurements and weight, and you can try several shapes at our showroom.

q: What jewellery should I wear with a gold, champagne or beige lehenga so it does not blend into the fabric?
a: Choose contrast rather than more gold: diamonds, or Polki set with emeralds, rubies or pearls, stand out clearly against zari. Pick one hero piece, usually the necklace, and repeat one stone colour in the earrings and tikka. Bring a photo of your lehenga to our Parle Point showroom and we will try pieces against it with you. Read more: /blog/jewellery-for-a-gold-champagne-or-beige-lehenga

q: Which jewellery set suits an engagement lehenga - a light Polki choker or a diamond collar necklace?
a: Both work: a light Polki choker suits a rich, traditional lehenga, while a diamond collar suits pastel, ivory or modern outfits and evening functions. Keep the engagement set lighter than the wedding set and choose pieces you can wear again. Every piece comes with its grading report and a BIS HUID hallmark on the gold. Read more: /blog/engagement-lehenga-jewellery-polki-choker-or-diamond-collar

q: What should I wear on my forehead and ears with a bridal veil or head dupatta?
a: A slim maang tikka in the centre parting, or a passa on one side, usually works best because both sit under or beside the drape without lifting it. Choose longer earrings to frame the face, and skip forehead jewellery if the veil has a heavy border. Bring your dupatta to our showroom to try the full look. Read more: /blog/maang-tikka-passa-or-nothing-with-a-bridal-veil

q: What jewellery can a groom wear with a sherwani?
a: Two or three pieces are enough: a pearl or Polki mala over the sherwani, one strong ring, and a kada or small diamond studs. Match the metal tone and one stone colour to the bride's set, and keep a brooch for the blazer at the reception. Gold pieces carry a BIS HUID hallmark and diamonds come with their grading report. Read more: /blog/what-jewellery-can-a-groom-wear-with-a-sherwani

q: What should I check when buying jewellery on Dhanteras or Diwali?
a: Check five things before you pay: the BIS hallmark on the gold, the 6-character HUID verified in the BIS Care app, an itemised bill with gold weight and stone details, the diamond grading report number (matched to the laser inscription on solitaires), and the exchange terms in writing. A good jeweller will happily let you check each one at the counter. WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 if you want us to keep pieces ready for you.

q: How can I check gold purity at home - are the magnet, acid or scratch tests reliable?
a: No, home tests are not reliable: a magnet only catches some obvious non-gold metals, and acid or scratch tests need training and can damage the piece. The dependable proof is the BIS hallmark with its HUID, which you can verify in the BIS Care app. For a precise reading, an XRF test at a BIS-recognised hallmarking centre measures purity without harming the jewellery. We show you the hallmark on every piece at our showroom.

q: Can I buy a loose certified diamond in Surat and have a ring made around it in a design I choose?
a: Yes. At Vaishnavi Jewels you choose a certified solitaire with its GIA or IGI report, match its laser-inscribed number under a loupe, then pick the setting, band and gold. We make the ring in our own manufacturing unit, in about 3 weeks (simple designs can be faster), and the gold mount is BIS HUID hallmarked. Read more: /blog/choose-a-certified-solitaire-and-design-your-own-ring-in-surat

q: What does fluorescence mean on a diamond certificate, and should it worry me?
a: Fluorescence is how a diamond glows, usually blue, under ultraviolet light, and reports grade it from None to Very Strong. In normal light most diamonds look the same whatever the grade; only occasionally can strong fluorescence make a stone look slightly hazy. The best check is to look at the stone yourself in daylight, which we are happy to do with you at the showroom.

q: What does eye-clean mean, and which clarity grade is enough for an everyday solitaire?
a: Eye-clean means you cannot see any inclusions with the naked eye at a normal viewing distance. Many VS and some SI stones are eye-clean, but it depends on the stone's size, shape and where the inclusions sit, so the grade alone does not decide it. Read the clarity plot on the report and look at the stone under a loupe and with your own eyes; we do this with you at the counter.

q: How can I find my partner's ring size secretly before buying an engagement ring?
a: Borrow a ring she already wears on the same finger and hand and have it measured, or trace its inside circle on paper. A close friend or family member can also find out her size casually. If the size is not exact, resizing is possible later and is free for a new piece bought from us, though rings with diamonds set all the way round are harder to resize.

q: Can I clean my diamond jewellery at home with soap, toothpaste or an ultrasonic cleaner?
a: Use warm water, a few drops of mild soap and a soft toothbrush, then rinse and dry with a lint-free cloth. Avoid toothpaste and other abrasives, which can scratch the gold, and avoid ultrasonic cleaners at home because the vibration can loosen stones; never use them on Polki or Kundan. Bring your jewellery to our showroom for a prong check and professional cleaning.

q: What is the difference between Polki and Kundan jewellery, and which one has real diamonds?
a: Polki is the stone: natural diamonds left uncut and set in gold. Kundan is a way of setting stones in fine gold foil, and the stones in Kundan work are often glass or other gems rather than diamonds, so always ask what the stones are. At Vaishnavi Jewels the bill names the stones in every piece and shows the gold weight and the stones separately, and every piece carries a BIS HUID hallmark. Our Journal guide on Polki and Kundan explains more, or WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 to see both.

q: Are Polki (uncut) diamonds certified, and what papers should come with a Polki set?
a: Polki diamonds are uncut, so they are not graded one by one the way a solitaire is. What you should receive is an itemised invoice that shows the gold weight and the stones separately, and a BIS HUID hallmark on the gold, which you can check in the BIS Care app; every Vaishnavi piece, Polki included, is HUID hallmarked. Ask our team on WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 to show you the papers for any set before you decide.

q: What does '0% or 100% off making charges' really mean on a jewellery bill?
a: Making charges are only one line of a jewellery bill, so an offer on making alone does not tell you the total value. Read every line: the gold weight and karat, the gold rate used, the making charge, the diamond or stone weight and quality, and GST, and compare the final total. Ask for an itemised invoice wherever you buy; ours lists the gold and the stones separately, and we are happy to walk you through any bill on WhatsApp +91 75674 00099.

q: Can I give my old gold jewellery and get a new diamond design made from it in Surat?
a: Yes. We accept old gold jewellery, including pieces from other jewellers, in exchange towards new jewellery, and because we make jewellery in our own manufacturing unit in Surat, the new piece can be a diamond design of your choice. Custom pieces take about 3 weeks (simple designs can be faster) once the design is final, and the new piece carries a BIS HUID hallmark. WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 with photos of your old pieces and the design you have in mind.

q: Is 14K or 18K gold better for diamond jewellery I will wear every day?
a: Both work well; the choice is about colour and feel. 14K has more alloy, so it is a little harder and resists scratches and bending slightly better, which suits rings and bracelets worn daily, while 18K has more gold and a richer yellow colour. We make diamond jewellery in 9K, 14K and 18K gold, all BIS HUID hallmarked, and you can compare them in the showroom.

q: What decides the value of a solitaire ring - carat, cut, colour, clarity or the certificate lab?
a: Mostly the diamond itself: its carat weight, cut, colour and clarity together, as written on its grading report, along with its shape and fluorescence, and then the gold and the setting of the ring. The laboratory that graded the stone is named on the report, so always check which lab it is. Every Vaishnavi solitaire is laser-inscribed with its GIA or IGI report number; WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 and we will explain each grade on the report of the stone you like.

q: I live abroad (NRI) - can I buy jewellery in Surat and carry it back, and what bills do I need for customs?
a: Yes. Many NRI families choose and buy while they are in India, in our showroom, and carry the jewellery back with them; we deliver within India only, not overseas. Keep the itemised invoice, which shows the gold weight, the HUID and the diamond report numbers, together with the grading reports. Customs allowances differ by country, so check the current rules of the country you are flying to before you travel.

q: Which diamond mangalsutra design suits daily office wear?
a: For daily office wear, choose a light mangalsutra: a fine single-strand chain with small black beads and a small diamond pendant that sits flat, with a secure clasp. A delicate chain in rose or yellow gold matched to the pendant is comfortable under collars and goes with both western and Indian clothes. Our Journal guide on choosing a diamond mangalsutra for daily wear explains lengths and care, and you can see designs on WhatsApp +91 75674 00099.

q: Can you send me photos of your Polki sets on WhatsApp before I visit?
a: Yes. Message us on WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 with the occasion and the style you like, and our team will share photos and videos of matching Polki sets. You can also see recent pieces on our Instagram, @vaishnavijewels.surat. Once you have a shortlist, book a visit and we will keep those pieces ready for you.

q: Can I see bridal choker sets in my budget before I come to the showroom?
a: Yes. Share your wedding date, outfit colours and the budget you have in mind on WhatsApp +91 75674 00099, and we will shortlist bridal chokers from our designs for you. If you want a change in size, stones or gold karat, we can make it in our own manufacturing unit, to suit your budget. Then book a visit to try the shortlisted pieces in person.

During the closure you can still WhatsApp us on +91 75674 00099 and we will guide you, and book a visit slot from 16 November. Normal hours are Monday to Saturday, 11 AM to 8 PM.

q: Is one bigger solitaire better than many smaller pieces for a bride this season?
a: It depends on how she will wear it after the wedding. One larger solitaire in a ring or pendant is a piece worn every day for years, while several smaller pieces give more variety across functions; carat, cut and setting together decide how large a stone looks. Every Vaishnavi solitaire has its own grading report and a laser-inscribed report number, so you can compare stones with confidence; WhatsApp +91 75674 00099.

q: How many days before a November-December wedding should I confirm a made-to-order set?
a: Confirm the design at least four weeks before the wedding: custom and bridal pieces take about 3 weeks (simple designs can be faster) from the final design, depending on the work, and a few extra days help for a trial and small changes. If time is shorter, our diamond and Polki pieces are in ready stock. Send your wedding date on WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 and we will confirm the timeline.

q: Is a diamond grading report the same as a jeweller's valuation certificate, and which one should I ask for?
a: No. A grading report is issued by an independent laboratory such as IGI, EGL or TGL and describes the diamond's weight, cut, colour and clarity, with a report number you can check online. A valuation or certificate printed by a jeweller is that jeweller's own document. We give you the laboratory report and our bill, not a separate valuation certificate. Every Vaishnavi solitaire comes with a GIA or IGI report and is laser-inscribed with its report number so you can match the stone to it.

q: Is HUID hallmarking compulsory for custom-made gold jewellery or very light pieces under 2 grams?
a: Under the BIS rules, gold jewellery sold by a registered jeweller must carry a HUID hallmark; pieces under 2 grams are among the few items exempted, and being custom-made is not an exemption. At Vaishnavi Jewels every piece is BIS HUID hallmarked, including light pieces under 2 grams, custom pieces and Polki pieces. You can check any HUID yourself in the BIS Care app.

q: Can I see a 3D design or sketch of my custom diamond ring or Polki set before it is made?
a: You see and approve the design before any work starts: the look, the gold karat and the diamond quality are agreed with you, from your photo, a sketch or one of our designs. For custom pieces we show you the sketch and then the CAD (3D) design to approve before it is made, and when needed we also show you the cast piece before it is finished. Because we make it in our own manufacturing unit in Surat, changes are easy at the design stage; WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 to begin.

q: How do I know my natural diamond is conflict-free, and what is the Kimberley Process?
a: The Kimberley Process is an international scheme, in place since 2003, under which rough diamonds traded between member countries travel with a government certificate stating they are conflict-free; along the trade, sellers add a warranty statement on their invoices that the diamonds come from legitimate sources. A grading report tells you a stone's quality and that it is natural, but not which mine it came from. Our Journal guide on the Kimberley Process explains what to ask for when you buy.

q: Can I get my old diamond ring tested or certified in Surat, and what happens if it was never certified?
a: Yes. A first check with a diamond tester and a loupe shows whether the stone is a diamond; for a full grading report, the diamond can be sent to a grading laboratory such as IGI, which records its weight, cut, colour and clarity. A stone set in a ring may need to be taken out for a complete report. WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 and our team will explain the steps and the time it takes.

q: Does a lab-grown diamond fade, turn yellow or lose its shine with time?
a: No. A lab-grown diamond is real diamond, so its colour and hardness do not change with time or daily wear. If it looks dull, it is usually a film of soap, lotion or dust, which comes off with warm water, mild soap and a soft brush. Every Vaishnavi lab-grown solitaire comes with a grading report and a laser-inscribed report number, so the stone can be matched to the same report years later.

q: Can I insure my diamond jewellery, and which papers do I need to keep for a claim?
a: Yes, many insurers cover jewellery, either on its own or under a home policy. Keep the original itemised invoice, the grading reports, a note of each HUID and clear photos of every piece, as insurers usually ask for these to value a claim. Confirm the cover, conditions and any valuation needed with your own insurer.

q: How do I choose a wedding band that sits flush with my solitaire engagement ring?
a: Choose a band shaped to the engagement ring: a curved or notched (contoured) band follows the setting, while a straight band sits flush only when the solitaire is set high enough above it. Match the width and gold colour, and try both rings together on your finger. Because we make rings in our own manufacturing unit, a band can be made to fit your solitaire; WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 with a photo of your ring.

q: My family has an old Polki set - can it be repaired, re-set or remade into a new design in Surat?
a: Often, yes. We make Polki jewellery in our own manufacturing unit, so our team can look at a family set and tell you honestly what can be cleaned, repaired, re-foiled or re-set and what is better remade into a new design. Old gold can be taken in exchange towards a new piece, and the new gold carries a BIS HUID hallmark. Send clear photos of the front and back of the set on WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 to start.

q: What necklace and earrings suit a jacket blouse or deep-back blouse lehenga?
a: With a jacket or high-neck blouse, choose a choker or collar necklace that sits above the neckline, with statement earrings; with a deep-back blouse, keep the front light and let long earrings or a back chain add detail. Pick one hero piece so the blouse and the jewellery do not compete. Our Journal guide explains each blouse style, and you can WhatsApp us on +91 75674 00099 for guidance.

q: What jewellery should the bride's sister or bridesmaids wear to the sangeet and wedding without upstaging the bride?
a: Choose lighter pieces from the same style family as the bride's set: a slim Polki or diamond choker or statement earrings, a few stacked bangles and a ring, in the same metal tone. Keep one piece as the focus and leave the full layered set, the large tikka and the nath to the bride. Our Journal guide has function-by-function ideas, or WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 to plan matching looks for the family.

q: What necklace works with a sharara or high-neck anarkali for a wedding function?
a: A short choker or collar necklace that sits just above the neckline works well, paired with chandbalis or long earrings to frame the face. Long necklaces tend to fight a high neckline, so keep them for open or V-necks. Our own manufacturing unit can adjust a necklace's length and clasp to your outfit; WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 to see options.

q: Is your jewellery real gold or gold-plated, and how can I check it?
a: All our jewellery is real gold - 14K, 18K or 22K - made in our own manufacturing unit in Surat. Every piece carries a BIS hallmark with a 6-digit HUID, and you can check that HUID yourself in the free BIS Care app. Your bill states the gold purity and weight. WhatsApp +91 75674 00099.

q: Can I get Polki jewellery made as an anniversary gift?
a: Yes. We make Polki pieces to order in our own Surat unit - a light pendant, earrings or a full set. You see a sketch or 3D design before it is made, and simple designs are ready in about 4 days to 3 weeks. Tell us the occasion and date on WhatsApp +91 75674 00099.

q: Is lightweight diamond jewellery strong enough for daily office wear?
a: Yes, when it is made well. For daily wear we use 14K or 18K gold (harder than 22K), secure prong or bezel settings and smooth edges that do not catch on clothes. Get the prongs checked once or twice a year - we do it free at our Parle Point showroom.

q: Will a lightweight diamond necklace look too small for a wedding function?
a: Not if it is styled right. Layer a lightweight necklace with a slightly longer chain, add statement earrings, or choose a design with more open space and sparkle rather than more gold weight. We help you build a festive look that you can still wear to work later.

q: Will my family be able to tell my diamond is lab-grown, and will my parents or in-laws accept it?
a: To the eye, a laboratory-grown diamond looks the same as a natural one - only a lab test can tell them apart. It is a real diamond, not a fake stone, and it comes with its own report. Many families accept it once they see the certificate. Our advice: be open about it, and choose what feels right for your family.

q: Can a jeweller sell me a lab-grown diamond as natural if I do not check the certificate?
a: It can happen, which is why you should always check three things: the report number on the certificate, the laser inscription on the diamond (we show it to you under a loupe), and your bill. Under the BIS rule IS 19469, a bill must say 'laboratory-grown diamond' for lab stones - 'diamond' alone means natural.

q: Can a GIA or IGI report or a laser inscription be faked, and how do I protect myself?
a: Fake paper reports do exist, so never rely on the paper alone. Enter the report number on the GIA or IGI website and check that the shape, weight and grades match. Then match the laser inscription on the diamond to that number. A good jeweller will happily do this with you at the counter - we do it for every certified diamond.

q: Will a lab-grown diamond lose its value, and should I wait before buying?
a: Lab-grown diamond prices have been falling, so buy one because you love wearing it, not as an investment. For long-term value, natural diamonds and gold hold better. We do offer buy-back and exchange options on our lab-grown and Polki jewellery - ask us for the terms before you buy.

q: How much is deducted when I sell back diamond jewellery - is it an investment?
a: The gold always keeps its value; the diamond part depends on the jeweller's buy-back terms, and buy-back is usually below the price you paid. Diamond jewellery is best seen as something to wear and pass on, not a pure investment. We offer buy-back and exchange - always take the terms in writing with your bill.

q: What does the new BIS rule mean - what should my bill call a lab-grown diamond?
a: Under BIS standard IS 19469 (from 2026), the word 'diamond' alone means a natural diamond. A lab stone must be called 'laboratory-grown diamond' (or 'laboratory-created diamond'), and the growth method such as CVD or HPHT should be disclosed. Our bills follow this wording.

q: Is an SGL or in-house certificate as good as IGI or GIA for lab-grown diamonds?
a: IGI and GIA are the most widely recognised labs, and their reports can be checked online by report number. Other labs and in-house cards vary a lot in strictness. For a solitaire, ask for an IGI or GIA report - our solitaires come with GIA or IGI reports.

q: Is it better to buy diamond jewellery directly from a manufacturer in Surat?
a: Buying from a maker means you can see how a piece is made, change the design, and ask the person who made it any question. What matters most is still the same: certified diamonds, BIS HUID hallmarked gold and a clear bill. q: If I order from another city, how is diamond jewellery delivered and insured?

q: Can I wear a diamond for astrology - does a lab-grown diamond work as a ratna?
a: Astrologers differ on this, so ask your own astrologer. Many say a ratna should be natural and untreated. Chemically, a laboratory-grown diamond is real diamond, but if you are buying for astrology, we suggest a certified natural diamond.

q: Is 9K or 14K gold real gold, and is it hallmarked?
a: Yes, both are real gold with a lower purity: 14K is 58.5% gold (stamped 585) and 9K is 37.5% (stamped 375). BIS hallmarks these grades with a HUID like other gold. Lower karat is harder, so it suits light daily-wear diamond pieces. Ask us which purity suits your piece.

q: Gold is very expensive now - how do I get a big diamond look with less gold?
a: Choose designs with open settings, fancy shapes like oval, pear or marquise that look larger, halo designs and 14K or 18K gold. Lightweight necklaces and studs give a lot of sparkle for little gold weight. We design for exactly this in our Surat unit.

q: What diamond jewellery can I buy with my first salary or bonus to wear to office every day?
a: Good first pieces are diamond studs, a small solitaire or halo pendant, a slim diamond band or a light tennis bracelet in 14K or 18K gold - all easy to wear every day. Visit our Parle Point showroom or WhatsApp +91 75674 00099 and we will show you options.

q: What diamond gift will my wife actually wear every day?
a: Pieces worn daily are simple and comfortable: diamond studs, a slim pendant, a light bracelet or a diamond mangalsutra. Think about what she wears most - office, home or travel - and pick something that goes with it. We can help you choose, and resizing of rings is free.

q: Is a diamond stud or ring for men in good taste for office?
a: Yes - small, clean designs are now common for men: a single diamond stud, a slim band with a few diamonds or a bold signet with a diamond accent. Keep it simple for office and choose a sturdy setting. We make men's pieces to order.

q: What diamond gift can I give my husband, brother or father?
a: Popular choices are a diamond ring or band, cufflinks, a kada or bracelet with a diamond accent, or a small pendant. For Bhai Dooj or a birthday, a ring or bracelet is always used. Tell us the occasion on WhatsApp +91 75674 00099.

q: Polki, Kundan or Jadau - which is worth buying for a bride who wants to re-wear it?
a: Polki uses real uncut diamonds set in gold, so it keeps more value and can be re-set later. Kundan usually uses glass or other stones with foil. Jadau is the traditional setting craft used for Polki or Kundan. For a set to keep and re-wear, choose Polki with a lighter design you can also wear to family functions.

q: Does Polki jewellery have any exchange or resale value?
a: Yes - the gold and the Polki diamonds both have value. We offer buy-back and exchange options on Polki jewellery; ask us for the terms and keep your bill and papers safe.

q: Should we choose the engagement ring together or keep it a surprise?
a: Both work. If you want a surprise, find out her ring size and style first (pins she saves, rings she likes). Many couples now choose together, so the ring suits her daily life. At our showroom you can try shapes and settings first; resizing is free.

q: What solitaire size do most people choose for an engagement ring in India?
a: There is no right size. Most people choose based on budget and what looks good on their hand. A well-cut, eye-clean smaller diamond often looks better than a larger, poorly cut one. Oval and pear shapes look larger for their weight. Try a few sizes on your hand before you decide.

q: Why is my white gold diamond ring turning yellowish?
a: White gold is made of gold alloy plated with rhodium, which wears off with time and shows the warmer metal underneath. A re-polish and rhodium plating makes it bright white again. Bring it to our showroom and we will check it.

q: Is a lab-grown diamond tennis bracelet practical for daily wear?
a: Yes, if it is well made: check that each stone sits in its own secure setting, the clasp has a safety catch and the links move freely. Take it off for the gym and heavy work, and get it checked once a year.

q: Which diamond nose pin is safe for daily wear - screw, press or wire?
a: A screw-back nose pin is the most secure for daily wear. Press and wire types are easier to put on but can come loose. A bezel setting protects the diamond best. We make nose pins in all three styles.

q: Can a diamond chip or crack if I knock it?
a: Diamond is the hardest natural material, but a hard knock at the right angle can chip it, especially at thin edges or points like pear and marquise tips. Settings that protect the edges, such as bezel or halo, reduce this risk. Take rings off for heavy work.

q: How do I check that a lab-grown report says how the diamond was grown?
a: A good lab report for a laboratory-grown diamond states the growth method (CVD or HPHT) and any treatment after growth. Look for these lines on the report, and check the report online by its number.

q: Should I get my engagement ring made in 22K gold?
a: Diamond rings are usually made in 14K or 18K gold because the harder metal holds the prongs and stones more securely for daily wear; we make diamond jewellery in 9K, 14K and 18K. If you live abroad, a family member can choose and approve the design in Surat, and we deliver within India with free insured delivery to a family address.

q: Why should I check a Polki set in daylight?

Ask for the gold purity (BIS HUID hallmark) and a clear bill as well. We are happy to show you any Polki set by daylight at our Surat showroom.

q: What is the difference between foil-backed and open-set Polki?
a: Foil-backed Polki is the traditional style: a thin gold foil behind the uncut diamond adds warmth and brightness. Open-set Polki leaves the back open so more light passes through the stone. We make both in our own workshop in Surat and can show you the two side by side so you can choose the look you prefer.

q: Is one fine Polki piece better than a bigger set?
